hook: Rumi was the most respected scholar in Konya. Then one day, he wrote this.

segments.en: I was dead... I came alive.
I was weeping... I became laughter.

segments.fa: دولت عشق آمد و من دولت پاینده شدم
segments.en: Love's fortune came, and I became fortune that lasts.

tafsir: Before Shams, Rumi had books, students, and honour. And still he says: I was dead.
Love was not one more thing he learned. It woke him up.
Now look at the last line. He does not say love's fortune came to me.
He says: I became that fortune.
Love did not give him something. It changed who he was.

outro.say: Part two. Who was Shams of Tabriz? Follow The Guest House.
